title: Rigveda 9.49: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.49: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.49 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 686r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.49.1-5 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 686r
translation.original_text:
1pava̍sva vṛ̱ṣṭim ā su no̱ 'pām ū̱rmiṁ di̱vas pari̍ | a̱ya̱kṣmā bṛ̍ha̱tīr iṣa̍ḥ ||
2tayā̍ pavasva̱ dhāra̍yā̱ yayā̱ gāva̍ i̱hāgama̍n | janyā̍sa̱ upa̍ no gṛ̱ham ||
3ghṛ̱tam pa̍vasva̱ dhāra̍yā ya̱jñeṣu̍ deva̱vīta̍maḥ | a̱smabhya̍ṁ vṛ̱ṣṭim ā pa̍va ||
4sa na̍ ū̱rje vy a1̱̍vyaya̍m pa̱vitra̍ṁ dhāva̱ dhāra̍yā | de̱vāsa̍ḥ śṛ̱ṇava̱n hi ka̍m ||
5pava̍māno asiṣyada̱d rakṣā̍ṁsy apa̱jaṅgha̍nat | pra̱tna̱vad ro̱caya̱n ruca̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1Poust down the rain upon us, pour a wave of waters from the sky, And plenteous store of wholesome fbod.
2Flow onward with that stream of thine, whereby the cows have come to us, The kine of strangers to our home.
3Chief Friend of Gods in sacred rites, pour on us fatness with thy stream, Pour down on us a flood of rain.
4To give us vigour, with thy stream run through the fleecy straining-cloth For verily the Gods will bear.
5Onward hath Pavamâna flowed and beaten off the Râkshasas, Flashing out splendour as of old.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 686r (numbered 3r by the scribe) (OPenn image 686, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.48.3 ‹rayim abhi rājānam sukrato›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 686v (numbered 3v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.50.3 ‹-harim hinvanti adri-bhiḥ pavamānam›. Verses 9.49.1-5 end on this page.

2tayā | pavasva | dhārayā | yayā | gāvaḥ | iha | āgaman | janyāsaḥ | upa | naḥ | gṛham
